items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1958-08-08; 1958-09-03
items.q: So you're a little older than Fess then, about four years.

ctx.x: So you're a little older than Fess then, about four years. I was going to ask while I think of it, that name Montutti, where did you ever get that name?

Well, I got that name. I'll tell you what we got that name. We used to play in the cafe, you know, nightclub. And this old guy used to come to hear us play. Pretty nice thought. He'd give us lots of tips, you know. And that was his name. They called him Montutti. Well, I was learning that name Montutti is called Duke. I don't know. Well, anyhow, O'Re and the boys, all this stuff. When the guy come in late, they say, come on there, old Montutti. You look just like Montutti. Well, they'd laugh at all. Johnny does,…

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: We saw him. We spent a lot of time with him.

ctx.x: Did you ever hear of a guy whose name is Manuel Mineta? Manuel Mineta, sure. Do you know him?

Oh, yeah. Manuel Mineta played violin and piano. Played trumpet. He's teaching now. We saw him. We spent a lot of time with him. He's teaching music now. He's a little over in Algiers. That's right. I don't know Manuel. Call him horse.
A lot of people still call him horse.

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: He just died about a month ago, Ed Garland told us.

ctx.x: The Dreamland right around the corner. Big store called Billings, Dreamland. We played, packed like sardines. We played, played. Money come on a Saturday night, they raid the place. They put everybody in jail, but they look at the band. They want to put us in jail, but the champions say, oh no, we didn't party. They didn't lock you up that time then? No. All right. Well, that was really bad, didn't they? That was going out of the field then. Going out of the field. All right. Well, got in the field. Well, they…

He just died about a month ago, Ed Garland told us. Poissy Wright died? Wasn't it? Wasn't he the one? I don't know where he is. No, that was the bouncer. The bouncer died. Who was the big chaper? Oh, you're talking about Zach Williams. Zach Williams died about a month ago.

Flo Walker. Big Zach. Yeah. He used to be a, used to wake and move it, yeah. He bought my memories up together now. Well, all right. Poissy, what are you doing coming out the depot? I said, I'm just coming over and looking at the race. He says, well, what's the trouble? I said, well, I'll show him a telegram. He said, oh, I'm sorry. I live on San Pedro Street. He said, I'll tell you what I'm doing. I'm going, we're going to make a trip all the way to El Paso tonight at 1130. And when you get over there, I connect…

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: Because we always did call him horse. All around the district. He was playing down the district.

ctx.x: I used to live over there. That's when I was taking lessons from Thess, Moneta. Moneta. Yeah, I used to take lessons from him. Manuel?
